post_hoc_leverage_check.file: novelty/prior_art/z_leverage.json (script z_leverage.py; post hoc, D_T2 already spent)
findings: The 'no-Z' comparator in confirm_d_t2.py (error 0.182) drops log Z without recalibrating the constant; a fair no-Z model recalibrated on the same T1 pool has error 0.122, i.e. at the 0.12 tolerance.

D_T2's ln Z differs from the T1 calibration mean by only 0.124. Any Z exponent between about 0.02 and 1.95 passes the 0.12 tolerance; the conditional bootstrap level interval [-0.078, 0.091] maps to exponents 0.37-1.74.

A constant T2 offset without Z, learned from A_T2, B_T2 (3 diagrams averaged) and C_T2, predicts D_T2 within 0.010 log, as well as the Z law (0.002). Z and the T1/T2 session batch are not separable here.
Within T1 the strict-law residual SD across diagrams is 0.118 log while the T1 Z range is 0.056 in ln Z; Z explains none of the T1 spread (B1 residual +0.16).

claims.allowed_wording_en: For one held-out string (D_T2) a locally frozen strict Schelleng prediction, F = cZv/beta with c calibrated on five T1 diagrams and the published Z, matched the fitted upper-boundary level within 0.002 log (conditional bootstrap [-0.08, 0.09]). This is consistent with, but does not establish, impedance scaling: the string's Z differed from the calibration mean by 12%, exponents of roughly 0.4-1.7 are equally compatible, and a tension-group offset without Z fits as well. Impedance scaling of the maximum bow force across strings has been examined before (Schumacher 1994; Schoonderwaldt et al. 2008; Mores 2016).
claims.allowed_wording_ko: 보지 않은 D_T2 한 도표에서, T1 다섯 도표로 상수를 정하고 공개 Z를 넣은 엄격한 Schelleng 식 F=cZv/β의 사전 고정 예측은 적합된 위 경계 수준과 0.002 log 이내로 맞았다(조건부 부트스트랩 [−0.08, 0.09]). 이는 임피던스 비례와 모순되지 않는다는 뜻이며 이를 입증하지는 않는다. D_T2의 Z는 보정 평균과 12%만 달라 Z 지수 약 0.4~1.7이 모두 같은 정도로 맞고, Z 없이 장력군 상수만 둔 모형도 같은 정도로 맞는다. 현 사이 최대 활 힘의 임피던스 비례는 이미 검토되었다(Schumacher 1994, Schoonderwaldt 외 2008, Mores 2016).

claims.claim: Sublinear speed dependence of maximum bow force is explained by thermal friction (mu depending on F*v).
claims.verdict: partially preempted: the thermal (temperature/power-controlled) friction mechanism and the statement that the maximum bow force depends on limiting friction and hence temperature are published; velocity-dependent modifications of Schelleng's maximum-force law are published. Not found: an empirical power law mu_d(F*v) from reconstructed bowed-string friction used to predict the speed exponent of the measured upper boundary.

closest_work.ref: Smith & Woodhouse 2000, J. Mech. Phys. Solids 48, 1633
closest_work.point: Rosin friction governed by contact temperature, not sliding speed; temperature set by frictional heating (citation only).

closest_work.quote: to deduce a maximum bow force requires knowledge of the value of limiting friction, and hence again the temperature
closest_work.point: Simulated Schelleng diagrams with thermal vs friction-curve models; no speed exponent of F_max derived.

closest_work.quote: combines influences from the contact temperature and the sliding speed
closest_work.point: Rate-and-state rosin model with heat balance; validated on Guettler (attack) transients, not on Schelleng speed scaling.

closest_work.ref: van Walstijn et al. 2026, Acta Acustica 10, 47
closest_work.quote: The results obtained with a specific steady bow velocity
closest_work.point: Thermal elasto-plastic model reproduces measured minimum and maximum bow force versus beta at one bow speed (0.1 m/s) on IWK data; speed dependence untested.

closest_work.quote: the slope of the upper bow-force limit in the Schelleng diagram increased with increasing bow velocity
closest_work.point: Attributed to velocity-dependent friction delta via a hyperbolic friction curve, F_max = 2Z0 (v_B + beta z0)/((mu_s - mu_d) beta); also found F_max approximately proportional to v_B on violin at 10-20 cm/s (deviation at 5 cm/s). No thermal attribution.
Best fit = Schelleng's model plus Schumacher's velocity term (form not read).

closest_work.quote: exhibits strong dependence on bow force but minimal dependence on bow acceleration
closest_work.point: Measured friction coefficients inserted into Guettler-limit conditions: analogous use of measured friction to explain playability limits, but for attacks; load-dependent friction is a competing explanation to power dependence.

closest_work.ref: Galluzzo, Woodhouse & Mansour 2017, Acta Acust. united Ac. 103, 1080
closest_work.point: Temperature-based friction models outperform sliding-speed models on measured transients.

claims.own_evidence_status: post hoc, one string (B_T2 friction reconstruction, Zenodo 15879128), 31 steady Helmholtz windows of which 20 are at 0.05 m/s; free fit mu_d ~ F^-0.182 v^-0.180 beta^-0.004 (equal F and v exponents, no slip-speed effect); power model AIC -194 vs force-only -146 vs slip speed -142. Predicted upper speed exponent 0.48-0.94 depending on force subset vs measured 0.49-0.86 across 10 diagrams. Temperature was not measured.
claims.allowed_wording_en: In a public friction reconstruction for one string, the mean dynamic friction coefficient during Helmholtz motion scaled as (F v)^-0.18, with equal exponents on force and speed and no dependence on slip speed v/beta. This pattern is consistent with power-controlled (thermal) rosin friction (Smith & Woodhouse 2000; Woodhouse 2003). Inserted into Schelleng's maximum-force condition it implies speed exponents of 0.48-0.94, overlapping the measured 0.49-0.86. This is a post hoc consistency check on one string, not a test of mechanism; velocity-dependent modifications of the maximum-force law were proposed earlier (Schumacher 1994; Schoonderwaldt et al. 2008; Mores 2016).
claims.allowed_wording_ko: 한 현의 공개 마찰 재구성 자료에서, 헬름홀츠 운동 중 평균 동마찰계수는 (F·v)^−0.18로 변했고 힘과 속도의 지수가 같았으며 미끄럼 속도 v/β에는 의존하지 않았다. 이는 마찰 일률(열)이 지배하는 송진 마찰 모형(Smith & Woodhouse 2000, Woodhouse 2003)과 부합하는 양상이다. 이 의존성을 Schelleng 최대 힘 조건에 넣으면 속도 지수 0.48~0.94가 나오며, 측정값 0.49~0.86과 겹친다. 한 현에 대한 사후 정합성 확인이며 기전의 검증이 아니다. 최대 힘 식의 속도 의존 수정은 이미 제안되었다(Schumacher 1994, Schoonderwaldt 외 2008, Mores 2016).
forbidden_wording: first explanation of the sublinear speed dependence

claims.verdict: novel as a specific quantitative audit of this dataset (not found), but only at association level; the 'predicted ... rather than string properties' wording is not supported after nested re-fitting and the D_T2 confirmation

closest_work.point: Lists rosin depletion, string tension variation and bow-hair tension; uses order-alternating repeats and remounting. Qualitative; not linked to Schelleng minimum-force levels.

closest_work.quote: no clear trend was peaking out
closest_work.point: Judges string differences against a same-day consecutive repeat (B T2), which cannot capture between-session variation.

closest_work.quote: the bending stiffness B of string D decreased by 29% after remounting
closest_work.point: Session/remount changes of string properties are documented, for attacks.

closest_work.quote: related to unsatisfactory control of bow force
closest_work.point: Considered whether force-control fluctuations bias the measured minimum force and concluded they did not; closest precedent of a protocol explanation of minimum-force results.
Minimum bow force has a baseline even at very low bow speed and depends on bridge resistance; a physical (not protocol) account.
Proposes F_min = C Z v/beta from simulated strings; our audit cautions against reading between-string measured minimum-force levels as string physics in this dataset.

closest_work.ref: Leek et al. 2010, Nat. Rev. Genet. 11, 733 (batch effects, generic)

claims.own_evidence_status: Post hoc over 10 exposed diagrams: r = +0.88 between lower level and dec5_pl (several session descriptors were screened: desc_b, dec10, acc_b, cal_low, cens, d0, fmin, floor, dec5_pl), string properties |r| 0.19-0.37 with negative LODO R^2. Association weakens on the nominal-force axis. Nested re-fit: level MAE 0.213 -> 0.101 but finite-column error 0.294 -> 0.316. D_T2 (pre-registered): primary level fit failed (zero-width interval, untestable); secondary column medians protocol 0.286 < mean 0.328 < log Z 0.376, all differences below the frozen 0.23 margin (indistinguishable).
claims.allowed_wording_en: Across the 10 analysed diagrams, between-diagram differences in the lower-boundary level were strongly associated with a session-level descriptor of the low-force load decrease (r = 0.88, post hoc), and more weakly with published string properties. The association weakens when the nominal force axis is used, it did not improve column-level boundary errors, and the one pre-registered test (D_T2) was not testable for the primary level fit. Lower-boundary differences between strings in this dataset should therefore not be interpreted as string physics without accounting for session protocol. We did not find a previous quantitative audit of this kind for this dataset.
claims.allowed_wording_ko: 분석한 10개 도표에서 아래 경계 수준의 도표 간 차이는 낮은 힘 구간 하중 감소를 나타내는 세션 기술자와 강하게 연관되었고(r=0.88, 사후 분석), 공개 현 물성과의 연관은 약했다. 공칭 힘 축에서는 연관이 약해지고, 열별 경계 오차는 개선되지 않았으며, 사전 고정한 D_T2 검증의 주 수준 적합은 검증 불가였다. 따라서 이 자료의 현 사이 아래 경계 차이를 세션 절차를 고려하지 않고 현 물성의 효과로 해석해서는 안 된다. 찾아본 범위에서 이 자료에 대한 같은 종류의 정량 감사는 발견하지 못했다.

reviewer_demands: Z vs batch: at least two further held-out strings whose Z differs from the calibration mean by more than the session scatter (~0.12 log), or a within-session design varying Z; report the fair recalibrated no-Z comparator and an interval for the Z exponent, not a single pass/fail.
Torsion: compare Z0 with the torsion-corrected Ztot (Schoonderwaldt 2008; Mansour 2016) using the POMA table's torsional entries; justify which impedance enters F_max.

Censoring: on D_T2, 63 of 111 scored upper columns were right-censored at the 4 N force ceiling; show sensitivity of the level fit to the censoring model and use the high-force parts (4-12 N) where finite upper boundaries exist.

Speed-session confound: every speed was recorded in its own session, so speed exponents (upper 0.49-0.86, lower) are confounded with session; need within-session speed variation or a session-adjusted exponent.

Friction: replicate the mu_d(F v) law on other strings; add an independent temperature or heat-flux proxy; test force-only (load-dependent) and slip-speed alternatives with held-out windows; note that 20 of 31 windows are at 0.05 m/s; propagate uncertainty to a predicted exponent with CI and compare per diagram.

Compare the thermal account against established alternatives on the same data: modified Schelleng with hyperbolic friction (v_B + beta z0), Schumacher's velocity term, and thermal-model simulations (Woodhouse 2003; Woodhouse & Galluzzo 2025; van Walstijn 2026) at the three speeds.

Shared force channel: the load-decrease descriptor and the measured-force boundary use the same sensor; demonstrate the association with an independent force reference or on the nominal axis, and model zero-offset drift (tens of mN up to 0.16 N).

Forking paths: several session descriptors were screened post hoc; fix one descriptor and its sign/slope and test it on unseen archives (B_T2 sample2, A3, A4, D2) with an external time-stamped registration (e.g. OSF), not only a local hash.

Independence and uncertainty: count independent strings and sessions, use session-level (cluster) resampling, and state that conditional bootstraps omit training, descriptor and new-session uncertainty.
Label validity: the H label is a bridge-force proxy; validate against the dataset authors' classification or a manual subset and report sensitivity to K, window start and amplitude threshold.
Novelty claims phrased as 'not found in the searched literature', with the unread_risks above checked (especially the Lampis et al. 2025 friction-reconstruction abstract and the Lampis thesis).
No violin generalisation: cello G2 monochord only.
